the apple green colour seen when a barium compound is heated in a flame
the reagent that gives coloured precipitates used to identify metal ions
the lilac or violet colour seen when a potassium compound is heated in a flame
items.s: Aqueous ammonia test: the reagent that gives coloured precipitates used to identify metal ions. The other options describe Sodium flame colour, Barium flame colour, Potassium flame colour.

items.q: The correct meaning of Universal indicator is
o: the scale from nought to fourteen measuring the acidity or alkalinity of a solution
a solution with a pH below seven
a solution with a pH above seven
the mixture of dyes, used as solution or paper, that gives a range of colours across the pH scale
items.s: Universal indicator: the mixture of dyes, used as solution or paper, that gives a range of colours across the pH scale. The other options describe Alkaline solution, Acidic solution, pH scale.

items.q: The correct meaning of Corrosive substance is
o: a reagent that destroys living tissue on contact, such as concentrated acids
the fitting used to flush chemicals out of the eyes immediately after a splash
a liquid whose vapour can ignite at ordinary working temperatures
an accidental release of a reagent that must be contained and reported at once
items.s: Corrosive substance: a reagent that destroys living tissue on contact, such as concentrated acids. The other options describe Flammable liquid, Chemical spill, Eyewash station.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Precipitate.
o: the apple green colour seen when a barium compound is heated in a flame
the strong yellow colour seen when a sodium compound is heated in a flame
the insoluble solid formed when two solutions react
the test in which a clean wire and a hot flame identify a metal by the colour given
items.s: Precipitate: the insoluble solid formed when two solutions react. The other options describe Flame test, Sodium flame colour, Barium flame colour.

items.q: Meniscus may be defined as
o: the sensitive balance that weighs to four decimal places
an error that varies unpredictably from reading to reading
how closely repeated measurements agree with one another
the curved surface of a liquid whose bottom level is read against the graduation
items.s: Meniscus: the curved surface of a liquid whose bottom level is read against the graduation. The other options describe Precision, Random error, Analytical balance.

items.q: In this course, Watch glass refers to
o: the flask calibrated to contain one exact volume at a stated temperature
the shallow glass disc used to cover a beaker or to hold a small sample
the squeeze bottle of distilled water used to rinse and to make up volumes
the instrument used to deliver one fixed volume of solution accurately
items.s: Watch glass: the shallow glass disc used to cover a beaker or to hold a small sample. The other options describe Wash bottle, Pipette, Volumetric flask.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Desiccator.
o: the vessel used for approximate volumes where high accuracy is not needed
the graduated tube with a tap used to deliver a measured volume in titration
the sealed vessel containing a drying agent in which samples are kept dry
the shallow glass disc used to cover a beaker or to hold a small sample
items.s: Desiccator: the sealed vessel containing a drying agent in which samples are kept dry. The other options describe Burette, Measuring cylinder, Watch glass.

items.q: In this course, Indicator refers to
o: the indicator that is colourless in acid and pink in alkali
the substance added to show the end point by a colour change
the point at which the reactants have combined in their exact mole ratio
the measured portion of solution taken for a titration
items.s: Indicator: the substance added to show the end point by a colour change. The other options describe Phenolphthalein, Aliquot, Equivalence point.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Tare.
o: the mass of an empty container that must be subtracted from a weighing
the digits of a measurement that carry meaning about its precision
a set of titre values that agree closely enough to be averaged
the curved surface of a liquid whose bottom level is read against the graduation
items.s: Tare: the mass of an empty container that must be subtracted from a weighing. The other options describe Meniscus, Concordant titre, Significant figures.

items.q: “the scale from nought to fourteen measuring the acidity or alkalinity of a solution” is the definition of
o: Acidic solution
Buffer
Alkaline solution
pH scale
items.s: pH scale is the scale from nought to fourteen measuring the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.

items.q: “the separation of a liquid from dissolved solids or from liquids of different boiling points” is the definition of
o: Crystallisation
Distillation
Filtration
Decantation
items.s: Distillation is the separation of a liquid from dissolved solids or from liquids of different boiling points.

items.q: The correct meaning of Aliquot is
o: the procedure of adding a standard solution until the reaction is just complete
the indicator that is red in acid and yellow in alkali
the measured portion of solution taken for a titration
the substance added to show the end point by a colour change
items.s: Aliquot: the measured portion of solution taken for a titration. The other options describe Indicator, Methyl orange, Titration.

items.q: Three of these relate to Volumetric analysis. Which one does not?
o: Titration
Potassium flame colour
End point
Standard solution
items.s: Every other option belongs to Volumetric analysis. “Potassium flame colour” belongs to Qualitative analysis, not Volumetric analysis.

items.q: “the point at which the reactants have combined in their exact mole ratio” is the definition of
o: Phenolphthalein
Titration
End point
Equivalence point
items.s: Equivalence point is the point at which the reactants have combined in their exact mole ratio.

items.q: End point may be defined as
o: the point at which the indicator changes colour in a titration
the measured portion of solution taken for a titration
a solution whose concentration is known exactly
the point at which the reactants have combined in their exact mole ratio
items.s: End point: the point at which the indicator changes colour in a titration. The other options describe Aliquot, Equivalence point, Standard solution.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Measuring cylinder.
o: the straight-sided vessel used for mixing and heating, not for accurate measurement
the squeeze bottle of distilled water used to rinse and to make up volumes
the instrument used to deliver one fixed volume of solution accurately
the vessel used for approximate volumes where high accuracy is not needed
items.s: Measuring cylinder: the vessel used for approximate volumes where high accuracy is not needed. The other options describe Pipette, Wash bottle, Beaker.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Analytical balance?
o: an error that varies unpredictably from reading to reading
the digits of a measurement that carry meaning about its precision
the sensitive balance that weighs to four decimal places
a set of titre values that agree closely enough to be averaged
items.s: Analytical balance: the sensitive balance that weighs to four decimal places. The other options describe Significant figures, Random error, Concordant titre.
